ns2:section.sectionText: This course will explore a selection of classics of ecological thinking (examples include Thoreau, Aldo Leopold, Edward Abbey, Rachel Carson, Arne Naess) and more recent contributions to facing our human plight and prospects for nature (possible examples include but are not limited to Wendell Berry, Wes Jackson, David Ehrenfeld, Dipesh Chakrabarty, Michael Serres, Vendana Shiva, Bruno Latour, E.O. Wilson, Ramachandra Guha, Rob Nixon), as well as supplemental material from conservation biology and environmental history. We will consider how these various ecological perspectives compare with classic and conventional accounts of economics, culture, and politics, including the most conventional or currently popular approaches to earthly problems and prospects. We will be less concerned to measure how popular or widespread a particular prognosis or recommendation for action, and instead assess their sufficiency to the problems we face.
